data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0; it is exp(-\u0398(n)). The finite obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations in which the bichromatic edges form a matching and every monochromatic component has minimum degree at least 2; equivalently, there is a perfect matching M' extending M such that G-M' is a 2-factor whose cycles are monochromatic. The expected number of such obstructions scales as exp(\u0398(n)), so their prevalence is exponential in n.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Fails if the random 3-regular graph has no perfect matching whose complement is a 2-factor with many cycles (impossible whp), or if the basin of consensus is exponentially larger than the basin of mixed states.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Fails if the process is not monotone in bichromatic edges.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The bichromatic edge set evolves by random star-toggling: a vertex with two bichromatic incident edges replaces them by the third, and a vertex with three deletes all three. This decreases the number of bichromatic edges monotonically. The absorbing states are exactly matchings. Since a random 3-regular graph has exp(\u0398(n)) perfect matchings and each perfect matching yields 2^{c(M)} stable colorings by monochromatically coloring the cycles of G-M, the number of mixed absorbing states is exp(\u0398(n)). The empty matching (consensus) is only one state, so the process is exponentially more likely to be trapped in a mixed matching.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
